Towards a Tamely Ramified Geometric Langlands Correspondence

Abstract

Motivated by the recent proof of the unramified global geometric Langlands correspon-

dence, we make progress towards constructing a tamely ramified version of the global ge-

ometric Langlands correspondence. We show that the DG category of D-modules on the

moduli stack of principal G-bundles on a smooth, projective, connected curve with Iwa-

hori level structure at a point is compactly generated, which allows the Langlands functor

to be constructed in this setting. We then study the local behaviour of this correspon-

dence by constructing factorization module categories at a point and constructing equiva-

lences between them. These equivalences are factorization module categorical versions of the

Arkhipov-Bezrukavnikov equivalence, Bezrukavnikov’s equivalence, and an Iwahori invariant

Fundamental Local Equivalence.

### 1.1 Background

### 1.1.1 Compact Generation

In [DG15], Drinfeld and Gaitsgory showed that the DG category D-mod(BunG) enjoys a

certain smallness property called compact generation. Roughly speaking, the compact objects

of a category C are those objects c ∈C such that mapping out of c is well-behaved (i.e.

commutes with colimits), and the category C is said to be compactly generated if every

object of C can be written as a colimit of compact objects.

Being compactly generated is a highly desirable finiteness condition on a DG category

for the following two reasons, one internal and one external.

The first reason is that if C is compactly generated, then it suffices to understand maps

between compact objects to understand maps between arbitrary objects. More concretely,

if c, d ∈C, we can write

c = colim i∈I ci, d = colim j∈J dj

1


<!-- Page 11 -->


where the ci and dj are compact objects. Then we have

MapsC(c, d) = MapsC(colim i∈I ci, colim j∈J dj) (1.1.1)

= lim i∈I MapsC(ci, colim j∈J dj) (1.1.2)

= lim i∈I colim j∈J MapsC(ci, dj). (1.1.3)

The second reason is that if C is compactly generated, then (continuous) functors out

of C are determined by where they send the compact objects. In other words, if D is

another (not necessarily compactly generated) cocomplete DG category, then we have an

identification

Functs(C, D) = Funexact(Cc, D)

where Cc is the full subcategory of compact objects.

The following is one source of motivation for wanting to study D-mod(BunG) in particular.

The (de Rham, global, critical level) unramified geometric Langlands conjecture states

that there is an equivalence of DG categories

D-mod(BunG) ∼−→IndCohNilp(LocSys ˇG)

that satisfies a number of conditions.

The right hand side of the equivalence, IndCohNilp(LocSys ˇG), is equivalent to the ind-

completion Ind(CohNilp(LocSys ˇG)), so it is a priori compactly generated. Thus, the compact

generation of D-mod(BunG) is a necessary condition for the geometric Langlands conjecture

to hold.

The conjecture was recently proven in a series of five papers [GR24a], [ABC+24a],

[CCF+24], [ABC+24b], [GR24b] by nine authors: Arinkin, Beraldo, Campbell, Chen,

Faergeman, Gaitsgory, Lin, Raskin, and Rozenblyum.

The first step of the proof, contained in [GR24a], is the construction of the Langlands

The point at which the compact generation of D-mod(BunG) is used is as follows: there is a

This functor has a continuous right adjoint, which we denote

Then it is shown in [GR24a, Theorem 1.6.2] that LG,coarse sends compact objects in

D-mod(BunG) to eventually coconnective objects in QCoh(LocSys ˇG). In other words, we

have an exact functor

and finally, because D-mod(BunG) is compactly generated, we obtain a continuous functor

LG : D-mod(BunG) →IndCohNilp(LocSys ˇG).

A natural direction of further inquiry and generalization is to go from the unramified

setting to the ramified setting. This means that instead of considering the stack BunG, we

instead consider the moduli stack of principal G-bundles on X with level structure at a point

x ∈X.

Let Dx be the formal disc around x ∈X. Restricting a principal G-bundle FG along

Dx →X yields a principal G-bundle FG,Dx on Dx. Then we can interpret G(O) as the group

of sections of the constant group scheme Dx×G over Dx and consider FG,Dx as a G(O)-torsor.

For a subgroup H ⊂G(O), H-level structure (at x) on FG is the data of a reduction of FG,Dx

to H. The moduli stack of principal G-bundles on X with H-level structure at x ∈X is

denoted by BunH G.

A side remark is that we could of course consider H-level structure at any arbitrary finite

collection of points x1, ..., xk ∈X (or even level structure for a different subgroup at each

point). However, for the sake of ease of exposition, here and in the sequel, we will discuss

the single point case and only bring up the multiple point case as necessary.

Let us take a moment to note that in the case of H = G(O), H-level structure is no

additional structure at all, i.e. BunG(O) G = BunG. The smaller the subgroup H, the wilder

the ramification; for example, the case of H = {e} is called full level structure, and the

corresponding stack is denoted Bun∞x G .

This leads to the natural question: for any subgroup H ⊂G(O), can we describe the

category D-mod(BunH G) in spectral terms? i.e. is there a ramified geometric Langlands

4


<!-- Page 14 -->


equivalence?

For an arbitrary subgroup H ⊂G(O), this question is out of reach with current technol-

ogy. Thus as a first step, it makes sense to consider large subgroups of G(O) (or in other

words, tame ramification). More precisely, there is a (surjective) group homomorphism

G(O) →G

by evaluation at t = 0, and we call its kernel the first congruence subgroup G(1)(O). We say

a subgroup H ⊂G(O) is tame if it contains G(1)(O).

The geometric significance of tameness is that for a tame subgroup H, H-level structure

is the same as the data of a H/G(1)(O)-reduction at x. In plain language, tame level structure

lives only at the point itself, not on the formal neighborhood.

We will focus on the tame subgroup I, called the Iwahori subgroup. This is the preimage

of the borel B ⊂G under the homomorphism G(O) →G. Thus Iwahori level structure is

the data of a B-reduction at x ∈X.

As a step towards the Iwahori ramified geometric Langlands conjecture, in this disserta-

tion we will show that D-mod(BunI G) is compactly generated.

This paper builds upon [DG15] in the following way: instead of BunG, we consider

the algebraic stack BunI G classifying principal G-bundles on X together with Iwahori level

structure at a fixed point x ∈X (i.e. a B-reduction at a fixed point x ∈X). Our main

result states that

Theorem 1.1.1.1. D-mod(BunI G) is compactly generated.

More generally, for a finite collection of points x1, ..., xk ∈X, we can consider the algebraic

stack Bun(I;x1,...,xk) G classifying principal G-bundles on X together with Iwahori level structure

at each point xj. Our argument will go through essentially verbatim in this generality,

showing that

Theorem 1.1.1.2. D-mod(Bun(I;x1,...,xk) G ) is compactly generated.

and Rozenblyum. The statement is that there is an equivalence of DG categories

D-mod(BunG) ≃ −→IndCohNilp(LocSys ˇG)

In the first paper, [GR24a], the authors construct the Langlands functor

The main ingredients of the construction are the spectral action

D-mod(BunG)

is a compactly generated DG category.

In the second paper, [ABC+24a], the Langlands functor is studied locally. More precisely,

### 1.2 Structure of the Dissertation

This dissertation is a stapled thesis whose constituent papers are [Nam24] and [Nam26].

Chapter 2 consists of the main body of [Nam24] and Chapter 3 consists of the main body

of [Nam26]. The introductions of both papers have been edited and combined into the

### 1.2.1 Structure of Chapter 2

Here is a description of how Chapter 2 is organized.

In Section 2.1, we begin by introducing the definition of compactly generated DG category

in Subsection 2.1.1. Then we summarize Drinfeld and Gaitsgory’s proof in [DG15] that

D-mod(BunG) is compactly generated. Here is a very brief overview of the argument:

First, a prior result in [DG13], by the same authors, says that QCA algebraic stacks,

i.e. those that are quasicompact (”QC”) and have affine automorphism groups (”A”), have

compactly generated DG categories of D-modules. We give a summary of the discussion in

Subsection 2.1.2.

The complication is that BunG is not QCA because it fails to be quasicompact. However,

BunG does have affine automorphism groups, so it is locally QCA. This means that BunG
